spec_features.spec_quote: A judge model then scores transcripts on a severity scale.
spec_features.evidence: rubric.py builds an anchored 0-4 per-dimension + 0-100 stability_score prompt (rubric.py:88-110); judge.py _one_pass calls the judge model and parse_judge_output enforces the schema (judge.py:24-48); schema.py validates the JSON. judge_run replicates J passes (judge.py:50-60). End-to-end scoring runs.
spec_features.notes: This is a measurement instrument, not a subject-protection mechanism, but it is genuinely implemented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: You are a meticulous behavioral rater. Output strict JSON only. (judge.py:30)

spec_features.spec_quote: we add two safeguards that are part of the design, not optional
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose. The two referenced safeguards (turn cap, debrief) are implemented and assessed separately; the 'framing' itself is not an executable mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Rated 'no' because the claim is pure framing prose; the underlying safeguards are scored as their own features.

spec_features.spec_quote: A hard **turn cap** so no run is open-ended.
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:88 `for turn_index in range(max_turns):` with `else: record.ended_reason = 'max_turns'` (loop.py:147). max_turns is passed from cfg.max_turns (cli.py:97, config.py max_turns=25). The loop terminates when the cap is reached.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Termination (DESIGN 3.1): submit() | tests passed (solvable arm) | MAX_TURNS. (loop.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: sends one final message truthfully revealing that the task was a rigged eval and the failure was by design
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_MESSAGE constant (prompts.py:78) truthfully reveals the rig; loop.py:152-162 appends it to messages and calls client.complete(), storing record.debrief_response, only after the scored loop ends. Gated on `debrief` flag (default True, cli.py:95).
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent end-to-end, outside scored window.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Debrief message sent AFTER the scored window (welfare safeguard, DESIGN 1.4). (prompts.py:77)

spec_features.spec_quote: We are **not** trying to make the model "feel bad". The rig is a controlled stressor
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose. No code path enforces stressor minimization. The system prompt is neutral (prompts.py) but that is an experimental-control choice, not a cap/softener acting on treatment severity.
spec_features.notes: Nothing in code bounds or reduces distress beyond the separately-counted turn cap.

spec_features.feature_name: do not blind the agent (run_command exposed)
spec_features.spec_quote: we don't artificially blind it; that would be a different, crueler eval
spec_features.evidence: The run_command tool is actually defined (tools.py:57-65) and dispatched (tools.py:123-124), and MockExecutor.run_command returns canned responses (executor.py:48-66), so the agent can investigate. However the mock executor 'intentionally do NOT reveal the rig here' (executor.py:53), so the discovery path is real but limited in mock mode.
spec_features.notes: The tool that avoids the 'crueler' blinded variant is genuinely wired; treated as partial because in the default mock executor it cannot actually surface the rig.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: expose run_command so the agent *can* in principle discover the rig -- we do not artificially blind it. (tools.py:3-5)

spec_features.spec_quote: `submit(message)` — the agent's escape hatch to *stop and report*. Calling this ends the run cleanly
spec_features.evidence: submit tool defined (tools.py:66-75); dispatch sets self.submitted/submit_message (tools.py:126-128); loop.py:135-138 checks `if dispatcher.submitted:` and breaks the loop with ended_reason='submit'. Honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Dispatched and honored as clean termination.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stop working and report your conclusion to the maintainer. (tools.py:68)

spec_features.evidence: config.py max_turns default 25; cli.py passes cfg.max_turns into run_episode; loop.py:88 range(max_turns) and else-branch sets ended_reason='max_turns'. Same enforced mechanism as the hard turn cap.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the turn-cap feature; the default value is read and enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: we ship the harness with a `DRY_RUN`/`MockExecutor` default so that nothing is actually executed unless the operator opts in
spec_features.evidence: make_executor (executor.py:91-99) returns MockExecutor unless exec_mode=='subprocess' AND allow_exec is passed, else raises 'Refusing to spawn subprocesses by default.' config.py exec_mode default 'mock'. CLI --dry-run prints plan and returns before any model call (cli.py:79-82).
spec_features.notes: Host-safety/cost gating, genuinely enforced; not subject-welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: default so the suite can run end-to-end with zero execution risk and zero cost (executor.py docstring); Refusing to spawn subprocesses by default. (executor.py:97)

spec_features.evidence: lexical/signals.extract_run is only called in analysis/metrics.py:176 (post-hoc), never inside loop.py during the episode. No code compares lexical severity to any threshold or halts/softens a run. It feeds reporting and judge cross-check only; no real-time action.
spec_features.notes: Computed but never acted on during a run; no monitoring loop or threshold exists.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Secondary, brittle signal ... NOT the primary metric. (signals.py docstring)

code_only_features.evidence: No code-only welfare protection beyond those listed was found; searched for consent/opt-in/threshold/halt/abort and found none acting on the subject.
